Name:  ___                Unit No:   ___
 
Admission Date:  ___              Discharge Date:   ___
 
Date of Birth:  ___             Sex:   F
 
Service: CARDIOTHORACIC
 
Allergies: 
Penicillins / Tobramycin / Bactrim
 
Attending: ___
 
Chief Complaint:
Progressive dyspnea, chronic tracheostomy tube.

 
Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure:
Bronchoscopy

 
History of Present Illness:
___ year-old woman with chronic tracheostomy. She has 
bronchopulmonary dsyplasia due to premature birth. She has had 
recurrent respiratory infections throughout
her life. She has not been able to be weaned from tracheostomy 
due to recurrent respiratory difficulties. For the past several 
months, she reports that she is more dyspneic with her normal 
activities. She is also endorsing dyspnea at rest.  She 
complains of chronic cough generally productive of white sputum 
but notes that it is occasionally green. She does not report 
fever, chills,
weight loss, or night sweats. She presents today for a rigid 
bronchoscopy to evaluate the upper airway with possible 
tracheostomy tube change to T-tube.

 
Past Medical History:
Tracheabronchomalacia
Bronchopulmonary dysplasia
Chronic Bronchitis
Asthma
GERD
premature at 26 weeks
Status post 4 airway reconstructions, last was at age ___, 
tracheostomy at age of 3 months. She has had trach tube removed 
several times, but required replacement because she could not 
maintain her airway.

 
Social History:
___
Family History:
Lung cancer in grandfather.  ___ cancer in
grandmother.  Mother: hypertension.

 
Physical Exam:
On admission
VS: Afebrile, 126/75, 76, 18, Oxygen saturation 98% on RA.
Gen: NAD, resting comfortably 
HEENT: MMM, O/P clear, sclera anicteric 
NECK: trachea midline, no stridor, Tracheostomy tube in place 
and
intact.
LYMPHATICS: no cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, no
thyromegaly 
Chest: CTA Bilaterally, no wheezes or rales 
CV: reg rate, nl S1/S2, no MRG 
ABD: soft, NT/ND, NABS, no HSM 
EXT: no CCE 
NEURO: A&O x3, 
PSYCHIATRIC: normal mood, no depression/anxiety 

 
Brief Hospital Course:
___ w/ chronic tracheostomy ___ bronchopulmonary dsyplasia from 
premature birth now s/p tracheostomy tube replaced it with a 
Portex 7-mm inner diameter, 9.9-mm outer
diameter, fenestrated, and uncuffed tracheostomy tube .  She was 
extubated in the operating room and monitored in the PACU prior 
transfer to the floor.

Respiratory: aggressive pulmonary toilets and nebs were 
continued.  

Voice:  POD1 her voice was very hoarse and weak.  On ___ she 
underwent Flexible bronchoscopy for Severe supraglottic edema 
and a ___ laryngitis. She improved with rest.

Consults: Thoracic surgery was consulted to to evaluate her 
candidacy for operative management of her bronchopulmonary 
dysplasia. They recommended further work-up to include 
esophageal pH testing, wire stent trial, and questionaires to 
further classify the patient's symptomatology.

GI: PPIs were started.  She tolerated a regular diet.

ID: She was started on Fluconazole for ___ laryngitis.

Pain: her pain was managed with PO pain medications

Disposition: Her voice improved with rest.  She was discharged 
to home with her mother and will follow-up as an outpatient.

 
Medications on Admission:
ACETYLCYSTEINE - 10 % (100 mg/mL) Solution - nebulize powder as
per directions three times daily
ALBUTEROL SULFATE - 0.63 mg/3 mL Solution for Nebulization - 1
treatment inh as directed as needed for sob

daily
NORETHINDRONE AC-ETH ESTRADIOL [MICROGESTIN ___ (21)] - 1 mg-20

OMEPRAZOLE - 20 mg Capsule, Delayed Release(E.C.) - 1 Capsule(s)
by mouth daily
SODIUM CHLORIDE - 0.9 % Solution for Nebulization - use inhaled
via nebulizaiton as directed
LORATADINE - 10 mg Tablet - 1 Tablet(s) by mouth daily

 
Discharge Medications:
1. Fluoxetine 20 mg Capsule Sig: One (1) Capsule PO DAILY 
(Daily).  
2. Montelukast 5 mg Tablet, Chewable Sig: Two (2) Tablet,

3. Ranitidine HCl 15 mg/mL Syrup Sig: One (1)  PO HS (at

4. Fluconazole 100 mg Tablet Sig: One (1) Tablet PO Q24H (every

Disp:*14 Tablet(s)* Refills:*0*
5. Oxycodone-Acetaminophen ___ mg/5 mL Solution Sig: ___ MLs

Disp:*300 ML(s)* Refills:*0*
6. Menthol-Cetylpyridinium 3 mg Lozenge Sig: One (1) Lozenge

7. Docusate Sodium  Oral
8. Omeprazole 40 mg Capsule, Delayed Release(E.C.) Sig: One (1) 
Capsule, Delayed Release(E.C.) PO twice a day.
Disp:*60 Capsule, Delayed Release(E.C.)(s)* Refills:*2*
9. Albuterol Sulfate 2.5 mg /3 mL (0.083 %) Solution for

Discharge Disposition:
Home

Chronic Trach
GERD
Bronchomalcia

 
Discharge Condition:
Mental Status:Clear and coherent
Level of Consciousness:Alert and interactive
Activity Status:Ambulatory - Independent

 
Discharge Instructions:
-Trach care as previous
-Humidified air 
-Complete Fluconazole 14 day course
-Throat lozenges for discomfort

-Sit up in chair for all meals. Remain sitting for 45-60 minutes 
after eating
-HOB slightly elevated at all times

Flexible Bronchoscopy ___. NOTHING TO EAT OR DRINK AFTER 
MIDNIGHT
